steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: I've been dreaming about the guerrillas again, Kassandra.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: This is the third time you've come to Endymion Temple to ask for a dream reading, Megas.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: You still dream of that night seven years ago?

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: Yes...

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: We hid in the forest on that dark night. The Sargonians surrounded the wood, hunting for us.

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: We could not make a sound, let alone risk a light. We had to disassemble our weapons in pitch darkness.

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: Screws, springs, Originium components... I tied the parts of my Arts Unit to my clothes and shoes, disguised as accessories.

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: The fear had me so cold that I did not notice when an Originium component had cut my palm open. I thought the wet stuff was sweat.

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: When the sun rose, we walked past the Sargonians, disguised as lumberjacks from a nearby village, about a dozen in total. We'd be dead if they saw through our disguise.

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: They sized us up. For a moment there, I thought the game was up. In my panic, I tripped over a tree root and plunged into the mud, face-first.

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: A Sargonian laughed and rapped on my shoulder with the hilt of his sword, disdainfully. But I was happy. I knew we were safe.

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: I keep dreaming about it. Do you think...?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: You want to know if it's a divine revelation?

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: Last year, I saw with my own eyes how the heroes spoke their will through you on the Agora.

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: You are the speaker of the heroes of Minos, and the only priest in Athenius who can tell a divine revelation from a normal dream.

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: If the gods will that I take up arms again, then I will... no matter how much I fear...

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Please sit down. Your legs are trembling and your face is pale.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: The heroes of Minos will not force their children back into a nightmare when they have already seen far too much of the horrors of war.

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: You mean...?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: I think you have misinterpreted the revelation.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Wisdom and courage shine upon you and your friends in place of the twin moons who closed their eyes, and delivered you in the morn, just as you woke up from dream to greet the beautiful Athenian dawn...

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: The virtues of the heroes should be praised, but the pain that has lingered for seven years has blinded you to the beautiful fruit that has ripened on the branches of fate...

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Pick it, for it is the heroes' blessing upon you.

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: A blessing... on an ordinary Minoan like me?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Our gods and heroes were once ordinary Minoans.

steps.name: Depressed Man
steps.text: Thank you, Kassandra. I'm beginning to understand...

steps.name: Acolyte
steps.text: I have come to relieve you, Kassandra.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: It's already time? So many visitors to the temple today.

steps.name: Acolyte
steps.text: You have so much on your plate, not just with visitors to Endymion Temple, but also acting on behalf of the head priest of Kereseira's First Temple in administrative duties while the position remains vacant.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: There's no need to worry about me, Folia. It is my calling to interpret revelation and speak on behalf of the gods.

steps.name: Acolyte
steps.text: So, you should know better than I do that the man's dream was mundane, not a divine revelation. To use more Columbian words—

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: He may have post-traumatic stress disorder. I know.

steps.name: Acolyte
steps.text: Why didn't you tell him?

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Divine revelation should be an honor for any Minoan, but there were only shame and fear in his eyes.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: He wants to receive guidance from the gods, but he fears that the nightmare is truly a revelation that he cannot refuse.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: If he believes in my interpretation more than he believes in himself, then I have a responsibility... to make his life a little easier, if nothing else.

steps.name: Acolyte
steps.text: I'll prepare some herbal tea with a soothing effect for him, and ask a doctor to follow up.

steps.name: Acolyte
steps.text: You have the afternoon off, don't you? You should stop spending it on the temple and focus on yourself.

steps.name: Kassandra
steps.text: Thank you, Folia. You take so much weight off my shoulders.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I'm so very sorry, Hekádemos.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I dozed off as soon as I reached the hotel. I didn't realize I would make you wait for a full three hours...

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: There's no need to worry, Kyría Mashayer. Waiting is part of the job for the Astynomos' Grammateús.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: You still look weak. Are you sure you want to visit the First Temple right now? You can rest a little longer.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Yes, I'm sure! If anything will bring me back to full strength right now, it's Kereseira's First Temple!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: I understand the original site of the temple was where Kereseira, the founding hero of Minos, first received divine revelation in the mountains.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: The first temple that she built there became the genesis of Minos.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: When Sargon... invaded Minos, they rebuilt the three great poleis as nomadic cities, but Kereseira's war-torn First Temple remained where it was.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Now, after a century, Athenius is rebuilding this temple, giving me the opportunity to see the historical building in its original form! This is incredibly exciting!

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: You are surprisingly well-versed in Minoan history... and surprisingly honest.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Unfortunately, the original plans of the First Temple have been lost, and thus cannot be perfectly recreated.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: However, there's quite a bit of 'classical' tradition in the way that they're building the temple.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: What do you mean?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: 'To revive the Minoan spirit, we must emulate the heroes who built Athenius, and build the temple of our own accord.'

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Before the referendum took place, these words by the original proponent moved everyone's hearts, and the vote on rebuilding the temple passed almost unanimously.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: No engineering blueprint, no staffing. Kereseira's First Temple shall be built through the passion of the Minoan people, and the veneration of the heroes that flows in their veins.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Wow! A living example of the Minoan spontaneousness that has driven so much artistic achievement!

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Thank you. I hope it's completed soon...

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Rebuilding in the classical style... how interesting! The proponent of the rebuilding must be an ambitious hero beloved by the people!

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Uh... how can I describe that Forte lady?

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: (Why is he taking so much time to think? Did you ask a question you shouldn't have?)

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: (Even if I did, I'm sure Hekádemos won't mind! He looks so nice, after all. Maybe he's choosing his words carefully, with a Minoan love of poetry.)

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Uh...

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Give me three seconds, Kyría Mashayer.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: O-Okay.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Three, two, one...

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Alright!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: You've thought of the answer?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: No, it's now five o'clock, and my shift is over.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Huh?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: I'll answer your question tomorrow, when I'm back at work. Enjoy your visit.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: But... we aren't even at the First Temple yet!

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: See those scaffolds? This street is a stone's throw from the main entrance to the temple. I'm sure you can find your own way.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Wait—

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Now, if you'll excuse me, I have a drinking engagement with a friend. He'll kill me if I'm late. Goodbye.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: You know, I was worried that the Astynomos' Grammateús would just take me around to see mundane tourist sites, leaving me with nothing to talk about when we get back.

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: You've got a way of smoothing things over for people, you know that?

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: If you ask me, I think the deferential-looking Liberi kid just enjoyed a three-hour break!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Well, no need to complain. There's plenty of time. Let's check out the surrounding area.

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: This is the land of heroes, after all. Maybe we'll walk out the door and straight into a heroic epic!

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: I knew it! You came looking for adventure!

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Rats, I came to you when I left the Grand Bazaar because I wanted a sugar mommy with money. Little did I know you were such a troublemaker...

steps.name: Mio
steps.text: Hey! Wait for me!

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Caught you!

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Keep your distance.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: That's no way to treat your old priest school classmate! I remember you were much more passionate back when we participated in debate competitions at Theros Temple.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Quiet down already. Loudmouth.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Looks like you know that I've come to debate you?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Don't worry, if you lose, I'll sing your defeat through a megaphone in standard hexameter.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Besides, you're the one who gave me the nickname 'Blaring Megaphone'. In return, I called you—

steps.name: Sober Craftsman
steps.text: Eloquent Rock! Blaring Megaphone!

steps.name: Sober Craftsman
steps.text: So glad the two great Athenian debaters are here! We're saved!

steps.name: Sober Craftsman
steps.text: Come with me! The apple farmers are making a scene in the temple, saying that the construction workers are delaying the quarrying to ruin this year's harvest by keeping the apples from sunlight.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: What about Pallas? The people may have chosen to build the temple of their own accord, but she was the initial proponent. Why don't you talk to her to resolve your disputes?

steps.name: Sober Craftsman
steps.text: Pallas has been crazy busy lately. No one's seen her since last night. Maybe someone else needed her.

steps.name: Sober Craftsman
steps.text: When people heard about it, they were all excited to emulate the heroes in building the temple, doing as much or as little work anyone had time for.

steps.name: Sober Craftsman
steps.text: Who could have thought that things would get so chaotic, even delaying the city's move to sunnier climes?

steps.name: Sober Craftsman
steps.text: Please, find us a solution through debate... or at least find us a loser!

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: I guess the two of us in a room naturally drives people to think of debate...

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: That's why I said—keep your distance, and keep quiet.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: How was I supposed to know? Just because you're smart doesn't mean you should skip the explanation and go straight to the conclusion!

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Actually, no, that's not right. I DID come to debate you. Everything works out!

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: I'm busy.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Always the same excuse after all these years. How on Terra did you win that debate championship with such a bland tongue?

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: You won't muddle your way out of this. For years, you've been running before I can finish the word 'debate'. Don't forget that there's still a competition we haven't settled!

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Come on, who are you arguing for? The fruit farmers or the temple workers?

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: You've known me long enough to know that I don't lie.

steps.name: Lykeion
steps.text: *sigh*... I'm going to the new Oripathy clinic to get medicine. Can you move?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: What...?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: Oripathy medicine? Didn't he pick up some last Wednesday...? Is he getting worse?

steps.name: Hekádemos
steps.text: I need to find out.

steps.name: Sober Craftsman
steps.text: Hey! Don't go!

steps.name: Sober Craftsman
steps.text: The fruit farmers and our guys are about to come to blows! Who's gonna solve our problem? We can't just pull some random soul off the street!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Look, Mio! So many people here in the temple! Looks like the Athenians are really excited to rebuild it! I feel like joining in myself!

steps.name: Titi
steps.text: Excuse me, sir. Are you looking for someone to help?
